name: Shimizu Robo-Buddy Ceiling
summary: A two-armed autonomous robot that drives to its work position using the BIM model, lifts a plasterboard to the ceiling frame with one arm and screws it on with the other; built by Shimizu for its own sites.

germany.statusNote: Not sold: Shimizu developed Robo-Buddy for its own building sites in Japan and plans to reuse each robot across two to three of its sites; no sale, rental or licence offer found.

specs.label: Length x width x height
specs.conditions: width 2,510 mm with outriggers extended (2018 spec)

specs.label: Gripping capacity
specs.conditions: robot section (2018 spec); whether per arm or for both arms is not stated

specs.label: Sensors
specs.value: camera, 2D laser displacement gauge, force sensor

specs.label: End effectors
specs.value: vacuum pads to hold the plasterboard; laser sensor and screwdriver on the other arm

notes: An operator sends the task from a tablet; the robot finds its position by matching laser data with the BIM model and drives to the work place on its own.
Works from an autonomous wheeled base with outriggers and a lifting platform; the raised-floor version is described as two arms on a four-wheel vehicle.
A second robot, Robo-Assist Ceiling, brings the boards; the 2017 release also lists inserting ceiling hanger bolts and assembling the ceiling substructure.
End effectors can be swapped; a raised-floor configuration (Robo-Buddy Floor) was trialled on two floors of SHIN-OSAKA DOI BLDG. No5 in September 2021 (not covered by this record).
Gripping capacity of 30 kg is not stated per arm, so armPayloadKg is left empty.
